title: TickTick Pricing in 2026 for Free and Premium Plans
summary: TickTick pricing includes free and paid options. See which plan suits you by comparing features, usage limits, and cost differences at each tier.
body_markdown:
## Automating TickTick tasks with Activepieces


Retyping the same tasks is what Activepieces is for. It's an open-source automation tool that can create TickTick tasks from a form, an email or another app.


It sits beside your plan choice and doesn't replace it. Anything TickTick limits on your account still applies to the tasks Activepieces creates, so a flow that floods a free list doesn't get around the list limits.


### When TickTick automation is worth setting up


When the same task keeps arriving by hand, set it up. A client fills in a form and you copy the answers into TickTick, or a flagged email becomes a to-do you retype.


If you do that a few times a week, a flow pays back its setup time. If your tasks start in TickTick anyway, skip it.


A flow that creates many tasks will also reach your plan's limits sooner, so check that before blaming the tool.


Treat any connector's claim to "create a task" as something to test. The only proof's a run against your own account, with your own list selected.


### A simple workflow example


Three steps make up the flow in the builder: a Typeform trigger labeled "New Submission", an AI Agent step labeled "Influencer Management", and an Asana action labeled "Create Task", which connect form submissions to Asana task creation through AI processing.


The steps are chained vertically, and a "Complete 2 steps" badge at the top tells you one is still unfinished, leaving the automation blocked until all steps are configured.


Why it is unfinished shows in the right panel. The Typeform trigger needs a "Connection" and a "Form", and it currently throws "Throws an error, reconnect or refresh the page".


Until that's fixed, "Test Trigger" has nothing to run against, and the other two steps never get real data, meaning you can't test whether the workflow actually works.


Read the screenshot as a preview of where you'll spend your time. The wiring's quick. Authentication's where it stalls.


For TickTick, you would swap the last step for a TickTick action that creates a task. The sequence is:


1. Connect the form and authorize the account, and fix any reconnect error here before going further.
2. Run "Test Trigger" or "Generate Sample Data" so later steps have real fields to map.
3. Map the answers into the task title and list in your TickTick step.
4. Submit a real entry and confirm the task landed in the right list.


Only after step 4 should you trust the flow with live submissions.


Activepieces is the better fit for anyone who wants to automate TickTick task creation without hiring a developer or building the flow by hand, judged on how little setup it takes to get from a described process to a working result.


You open the built-in chat, describe the process that touches your connected apps, and what it publishes is a live flow in your account with a run trace showing exactly what happened.


The plan limits that TickTick applies still hold either way, so the advantage is in removing the retyping, not in getting around those limits.
